To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the preferential migration direction of Dictyostelium discoideum in response to an electric field can be switched from the cathode to the anode by inhibiting phosphatidylinositols-3-OH kinase and that this switching is mediated by guanylyl-cyclase and cyclic guanosine-3′-5′-monophosphate.
the direction of migration in electrotaxis can be reversed by manipulating the cGMP and phosphatidyinositol signaling pathways.
a parallel signaling pathway, in which multiple signaling cascades act in a coordinated manner, is required to switch the preferred direction of migration in response to an electric field.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanism of the directional switching in electrophoresis and electrotaxis.
the mechanisms of cell migration and the role of cGMP in cell signaling.
how cells sense and respond to extracellular electric signals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a combination of the inhibition of PI-3 kinase and cGMP signaling via GbpC is required for cathode-directed migration, whereas the N-terminus of sGC is involved in anode-directed migration in conjunction with the inhibition of PI(3) kinase and cGmp production.

the directionality of migration in electrotaxis is controlled by the balance between two parallel signaling pathways, one of which is PI3K-dependent and the other is PI3K-independent, and that the direction of the electric field determines the pathway that dominates.

the PI3K-dependent signaling pathway is involved in the cathode-directed migration of Dictyostelium discoideum under an electric field and that the N-terminal domain in sGC and the catalytic domains in both sGC and GbpC are required to mediate the anode-directed migration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the cGMP-GbpC pathway is involved in the cathode-directed migration, whereas the N-terminally truncated sGC (NtsGC) is responsible for anode-directed migration in conjunction with both cGMP production and PI3K inhibition.
a cell has multiple pathways to interpret an electrical cue and that the pathways are not mutually exclusive, but rather are integrated into the same cell.
the PI3K-dependent pathways and the sGC-dependent pathway are involved in cathode directed migration, whereas both the PI3K- and sGC-dependent pathways are required for anode directed migration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the direction of migration in response to electric signals can be switched by modulating cGMP signaling.
the direction of migration during electric-signal-induced migration can be switched by modulating cGMP and PI3K signaling in Dictyostelum cells.
the signaling pathways involved in electric-signal transduction are not linear but rather parallel, and that the direction of migration can be reversed by switching the signaling pathways.
